data.narrative:
Space42, a publicly listed Space & Aerospace company formed through the merger of Bayanat and Yahsat, has raised $695M+ in ECA financing. The sector comprises 13 peer companies across public and private markets: 5 public comparables (RKLB, PL, LUNR, ASTS, SATL) and 8 private peers including SpaceX, Rocket Lab, ICEYE, Sierra Space, and Planet Labs.

Standard valuation methodologies face material constraints. Peer-median multiples analysis is inapplicable due to insufficient narrow-stage comparables within Space & Aerospace—while 14 same-sector peers exist, filtering for stage-aligned or valuation-tier matches yielded fewer than the required 3 datapoints for reliable median derivation. Public-comp anchoring via P/S multiples cannot be executed; the Space & Aerospace public median stands at 27.4x across the 6-ticker universe, but Space42's revenue remains undisclosed, precluding multiple application. This revenue opacity is typical for private-stage aerospace entities and remains a constraint even post-listing.

The analysis highlights a structural gap in valuation support for Space42. Without disclosed revenue figures or a sufficiently dense same-stage peer set, neither multiples-based triangulation nor precedent transaction analysis can be reliably applied. Forward valuation would require either: (i) Space42 revenue disclosure, enabling public-multiple anchoring; or (ii) recent transaction data from comparable-stage aerospace financings. Current data is insufficient to support a quantified valuation range.
